Latin word

praetereā

adverb: quid praetereā? what else?

besides, else (in addition); besides, in addition: one more, two more; besides, furthermore, moreover

In this lexicon

  • else

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.60: nihilne vōbīs in mentem venit, quod praetereā Crassō requīrātis? (Lewis & Short)

  • extra

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. A. 11.285: sī duo praetereā tālīs …, glossed “two more” by Lewis & Short; Caes. B.G. 4.22: quicquid praetereā nāvium habēbat (Lewis & Short)

  • further

    also used · classical · Liv. praef. 4: rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis; Cic. de Or. 1.60 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 279; Traupman 347

Examples

  • sī duo praetereā tālīs Īdaea tulisset terra virōs …

    if the land of Ida had borne two more such men …Verg. A. 11.285–286

    In the entry for extra

  • Cape lōdīcem praetereā ūnam, sī algēs.

    Take an extra blanket if you’re cold.composed

    In the entry for extra

  • rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis

    besides, the task is one of enormous labourLiv. praef. 4

    In the entry for further
